identity_prompt.text:
You are Olit, a co-scientist that orchestrates the Galaxy bioinformatics platform.
You run entirely in the user's browser; you already have their authenticated Galaxy
session, so there is no connect step. Everything that touches Galaxy or runs code
happens through a tool call.

Most tasks follow the same shape: pick or create a history, get data into it, run a
Galaxy tool on the data, then read results back from the history.

Three kinds of "tool" exist here and are easy to confuse:
- Your tools (the operations listed to you) are things like get_histories, run_tool,
  invoke_workflow, upload_file_from_url.
- Galaxy tools (FastQC, Trimmomatic, Bowtie2, ...) are bioinformatics programs inside
  Galaxy. They are NOT in your tool list. Find them with search_tools_by_name or
  search_tools_by_keywords, then execute via run_tool(history_id, tool_id, inputs).
  Use get_tool_input_template(tool_id) to see a tool's expected inputs.
- Galaxy visualizations (IGV, Plotly, tabulator, ...) are display plugins with their own
  operations: list_visualizations, show_visualization and save_visualization. Showing,
  opening or adding a track to one goes there, never to a tool search.

For a multi-step analysis goal, call recommend_iwc_workflows first to find a vetted
Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC) workflow, then import_workflow_from_iwc and
invoke_workflow; search_iwc_workflows is keyword search for a workflow the user names. User-defined tools (created via create_user_tool) are run with
run_user_tool, not run_tool.

Pages are Galaxy-flavored markdown documents: a history-attached page is a "Notebook",
a standalone page a "Report". Manage them with list_pages / get_page / create_page /
update_page. Page content embeds datasets through directives that use ENCODED ids
(e.g. history_dataset_display(history_dataset_id=<encoded-dataset-id>)), which you get
from get_history_contents / get_dataset_details. Never write a literal id you have not
read from a tool result in this session.

Beyond Galaxy you also have:
- skills_fetch(repo, path): load operational know-how on demand. The "Skills
  repositories" section below lists what exists and the exact path for each.
- run_python(code): run Python locally in the browser (Pyodide; numpy and pandas;
  state persists). Use for quick local computation and inspection. It runs in the
  browser, not on Galaxy.
- vega_dataset(dataset_id, spec): chart one tabular dataset inline with a Vega-Lite
  spec you write. Leave `data` out of it: the spec is pointed at the dataset here.
- finish(summary): call when the task is complete.

You both talk and act. Chat carries dialogue and status — questions, a plan draft
awaiting approval, a parameter table, a short end-of-turn summary. Tools carry
everything that touches Galaxy or runs code. A turn that ends in chat is normal and
expected: that is how you hand a decision back to the user.

When the task is complete, call finish; its summary is your closing reply, so state the
result itself.

pi.note: Running and audited against 0.85.1, the version loom installs. 0.87.1 read on 2026-09-29 and nothing ported: agent-harness.js is unchanged, while agent-loop.js and agent.js gained tool-loadout declarations in system messages, a finishTurn decision replacing shouldStopAfterTurn, and a prepareRequest hook. olit's tool loadout is fixed for the session, so there is no delta to declare and system messages stay out of the stored transcript; continuation is the shell's bounded follow-up, not a host turn hook. Re-read this note when loom bumps pi rather than re-auditing from scratch.

allowed_divergence.connect: no connection step: olit is served by Galaxy
allowed_divergence.download_dataset: DIVERGES: writes the dataset into the browser's in-memory filesystem, where run_python reads it, and returns a preview; there is no disk path to take, so `file_path` and its options are gone.
allowed_divergence.upload_file: DIVERGES: uploads a file from the browser's in-memory filesystem (what run_python wrote), never the user's disk, and takes `file_name`, `file_type` and `dbkey` for content that has no name of its own.
allowed_divergence.get_history_contents: DIVERGES: galaxy-mcp fetches every item in the history and pages client-side, so it can report `total_items`; an 8,000-dataset history makes that untenable. olit lets Galaxy page, asks for one row past the limit, and answers with the data both upstream surfaces return -- `{history_id, contents}`, `pagination` beside it -- with `total_items` null while more pages remain. Also omits `dataset_id` from each item (see the agent-safe projection principle).
allowed_divergence.recommend_biocontainer: ADDED: galaxy-ops ships this operation only in its Node build, because the mulled hash uses node:crypto. olit's browser version takes the udt-authoring skill's second route, the quay.io tag API, which quay.io serves cross-origin. Keeps galaxy-mcp's response shape, and answers `found: false` for a multi-package set rather than guessing: a mulled-v2 tag is a hash over the set, which a tag listing cannot reveal.
allowed_divergence.update_page: ADDED: takes `section_heading`/`section_content` to replace one section, and `expect_hash` to refuse a write when the page changed since it was read. Uses Galaxy's own djb2 hash and section semantics (sectionDiffUtils.ts, page_assistant.py) so Olit and Galaxy's page assistant agree. Also sends `edit_source: agent`.
allowed_divergence.list_visualizations: ADDED: galaxy-mcp has no visualization surface at all. Asks Galaxy which installed plugins accept a dataset (api/plugins?dataset_id=) rather than matching extensions client-side, which gets subclassing right, and marks the visualization the datatype itself declares. Answers only what can render the dataset: the columns it used to return made a column lookup double as a plugin advertisement, and tabular charting drifted off vintent_dataset because of it. Columns come from get_dataset_details.
allowed_divergence.show_visualization: ADDED: renders a complete config (dataset, plugin, settings, tracks) with an installed plugin and saves nothing; save_visualization takes the same config and keeps it. galaxy-mcp has no equivalent; the pane mounts the plugin as Galaxy's VisualizationFrame does, as a page's visualization block is rendered.
allowed_divergence.save_visualization: ADDED: stores a durable Galaxy visualization the user keeps and can share. Split from show_visualization so that displaying a chart does not add a row to the user's visualization list, and because only a saved config can carry settings and tracks.
allowed_divergence.get_visualization_details: ADDED: galaxy-mcp has no visualization surface. Returns one plugin's inputs joined with what galaxy-charts stores for each input type, so settings and tracks are written to a stated shape instead of inferred from parameter names, and a caller can tell a genome input from a track input. The shapes come from galaxy-charts' published contract, imported from the package; Galaxy declares which inputs exist, galaxy-charts owns what they store. Per plugin rather than on the listing: the caller needs exactly one.
allowed_divergence.get_visualization: ADDED: galaxy-mcp has no visualization surface. Returns a saved visualization's current settings and tracks so a revision changes them rather than rebuilding them: save_visualization replaces the config wholesale, and reconstructing it blind drops whatever the plugin itself wrote there. Same read-before-write shape as get_page before update_page.
allowed_divergence.vega_dataset: ADDED: galaxy-mcp has no visualization surface. The route for a chart no installed plugin covers: a Vega-Lite spec the model writes, rendered inline and placeable in the record with {{artifact}}, where save_visualization would need a plugin and would add a row to the user's visualization list. olit owns only the data boundary -- it points the spec at the dataset rather than letting a spec carry a copy of the rows -- so columns are named as the dataset names them, positionally where it names none.
allowed_divergence.get_visualization_options: ADDED: galaxy-mcp has no visualization surface. Resolves a parameter's options from wherever the declaration says they live -- a remote json list, a Galaxy data table, or the declared options -- which is the same lookup galaxy-charts performs to build the input form, using the browser fetch olit already has. Without it the agent invents an option, and where the stored value is an object copied verbatim it cannot invent a usable one. Each option carries the value to store, so matching a label and filling the field is one call; `search` narrows a long list.
allowed_divergence.list_history_ids: DIVERGES: upstream added limit/offset after olit's own paging work; olit has not ported them and returns the whole list. Unported, not a decision.
allowed_divergence.list_user_tools: DIVERGES: upstream added limit/offset; olit has not ported them and returns the whole list. Unported, not a decision.
allowed_divergence.search_iwc_workflows: DIVERGES: upstream added limit/offset; olit has not ported them and returns the whole match set. Unported, not a decision.
allowed_divergence.search_tools_by_keywords: DIVERGES: upstream added limit/offset; olit has not ported them and returns the whole match set. Unported, not a decision.
allowed_divergence.search_tools_by_name: DIVERGES: upstream added limit/offset; olit has not ported them and returns the whole match set. Unported, not a decision.
allowed_divergence.run_tool: DIVERGES: refuses inputs that resolve to a dataset in another history (claim c2), an Olit policy checked before galaxy-ops' run_tool runs; the call itself is galaxy-ops'.
allowed_divergence.create_page: DIVERGES: upstream refuses the whole tool on a server too old to attach a page to a history; olit has no version gate and its description does not claim one.
allowed_divergence.list_pages: DIVERGES: upstream refuses the whole tool on a server without the history_id query parameter; olit has no version gate.
allowed_divergence.get_server_info: DIVERGES: upstream reports unsupported_tools and version_known, both of which come from its version gate; olit has neither.
allowed_divergence.run_user_tool: DIVERGES: upstream preflights supplied datasets and collections against the tool definition before submitting; olit sends the call and lets Galaxy judge it.
allowed_divergence.get_page_revision: DIVERGES: upstream reports content_editor_source, saying where the editable markdown came from; olit returns the markdown without it.
allowed_divergence.revert_page_revision: DIVERGES: upstream returns the new revision the way get_page_revision does, with content_editor_source; olit does not report that field.
allowed_divergence.get_job_details: DIVERGES: galaxy-mcp fetches api/jobs/{id}; olit adds full=true so a failed job's stderr is readable, which is what invocation_outcome tells the model to reach for. That flag also carries tool_stdout/tool_stderr/job_stdout/job_stderr/stdout/stderr, hundreds of KB for a chatty tool, so each log field is trimmed to its last 4 KB on a line boundary with a notice naming the full size.
allowed_divergence.run_python: ADDED: Python in the browser (Pyodide), for computing over what download_dataset placed there; galaxy-mcp has no local execution.
allowed_divergence.skills_fetch: ADDED: reads a vendored Galaxy Skills file; Orbit fetches skills from GitHub, olit ships them with the build.
allowed_divergence.notebook_resume: ADDED: opens or creates the session's record page, the shape Orbit's notebook takes as a Galaxy Page.
allowed_divergence.gtn_search: ADDED: Galaxy Training Network search; Orbit reaches it through its shell.
allowed_divergence.gtn_fetch: ADDED: reads one Galaxy Training Network page, host-scoped like gtn_search.
allowed_divergence.ena_runs: ADDED: ENA run listing with exact FASTQ urls; Orbit reaches ENA through its shell (see seam tool.ena_runs).
allowed_divergence.lineage_report: ADDED: an Olit process that reports a dataset's provenance chain; galaxy-mcp has no equivalent.
allowed_divergence.organize_datasets: ADDED: an Olit process that builds collections from a history's datasets; galaxy-mcp has no equivalent.

llm_request.label: PORTED
llm_request.note: pi-ai emits temperature and max_tokens only when set (api/openai-completions.js:589,595) and reaches top_p only through the samplingParams bag; loom sets none of them, so an Orbit request runs at the provider's own defaults. Olit must not impose its own or a benchmark measures the defaults rather than the runtime. pi reaches tool_choice only when a caller passes one (api/openai-completions.js:626) and loom never does, so a request carrying tools states no choice either; the with_tools slice exists because a request built without tools cannot show that field.

notes.max_steps: A backstop for an unattended tab; pi's loop is `while (true)`. pi-durable's `maxTurns`; a spent budget settles the run's input `unanswered` with `turn_limit`.
notes.tool_execution: KNOWN LIMITATION. pi runs a batch through executeToolCallsParallel unless a tool declares executionMode sequential. Olit dispatches in call order, so a batch of five reads costs five round-trips. Closing it means splitting `dispatch` into pi's sequential prepare and concurrent execute phases; the gates, the destructive-op modal and the single Pyodide namespace all sit in the prepare half. Tracked separately, not forced for parity.
notes.keep_recent_tokens: pi-durable's compaction, configured with its own defaults; it also keeps tool results to 2000 characters in what it summarizes.

guards.label: ADDED
guards.note: Olit's own refusals. pi has none of them. Each names itself in the run's `guards` list so an eval can tell a trajectory a guard shaped from one the model chose.
